scope: Teacher advice supplied in this chat; not an official assessment rubric

items.recommendation: Preserve the methodological strengths of the original proposal
items.assessment: Official folds, paired mixtures, training isolation, macro-F1 and cost measurements are all retained.
Compare failures under nonspecific noise and labelled competing events, and test augmentation transfer.
Use When Background Noise Has Meaning with a subtitle on semantic interference.

items.recommendation: Real environments contain multiple meaningful sounds
items.assessment: Used as the research motivation; the experiments remain controlled two-source mixtures.
Cited in the report, with its focus on speech perception and reasoning tasks noted; it is not treated as an ESC classification baseline.
Mix-CLAP is discussed in the literature review; no reproduction is claimed.
Frozen LAION-CLAP has completed clean evaluation and both full interference evaluations.
Weights are fixed, with no fine-tuning.
The 92-dimensional features include RMS, ZCR, centroid, spread, roll-off, flux, MFCCs and deltas.
The supervised baseline is retained, with 36,258 parameters.
SVM, a task-trained CNN and a pretrained audio-language representation are all retained.

items.recommendation: Avoid framing the study as a best-model contest or a fair training comparison
items.assessment: Study failure mechanisms and deployment behaviour, and explain CLAP's external pretraining advantage.
White noise, DEMAND backgrounds and labelled ESC events; the last group is split into same- and different-category distractors.
Both sounds may correspond to labels; DEMAND may also contain recognisable events.

items.recommendation: Check whether power alone explains failure
items.assessment: Compare failures at fixed nominal relative power without treating this as causal isolation of semantics. All 47,991 spectral/temporal descriptor records and acoustically matched subsets of the same targets are complete; residual differences still do not establish a causal semantic effect.
Use SNR for noise and SIR for competing events.
Use the same held-out fold, different fine classes and source recordings, at +10, +5 and 0 dB.
Explicitly treat equal-power mixtures as a stress test with single-label ambiguity. Add the four top-2 outcomes and top-1/3/5 sensitivity checks while retaining the original single-label stress test.
The main paired analysis uses +5 dB; complete curves retain all three levels.
Both pairing types are complete; coarse categories are not a quantified perceptual distance.

items.recommendation: Use fixed pairing rather than exhaustive combinations
items.assessment: Each target has one fixed pair per semantic condition; pairing randomness can be examined in future replication.

items.recommendation: Keep distractor recordings out of supervised training folds
items.assessment: Test distractors come from the target's held-out fold; source recordings spanning folds are also excluded as distractors.
Identity, class, category group, power, offset, gain, seed, hashes and overlap are all recorded.

Distinguish target, distractor and other classes, and add changes from gain-matched control to mixture. Exact top-k readout and clean gain-matched controls distinguish first-place capture from target rank retention.

The denominator is the number of errors; also report the capture fraction across all trials and raw counts. Separately report the fraction of captures retaining the target in the top two, with its denominator distinguished from all trials.

items.recommendation: CLAP target and distractor text scores
items.assessment: Save cosine scores for all 50 classes and examine target–distractor competition.
Use SVM decision scores, CNN logits and CLAP cosines; do not compare absolute scales across models.
Boxplots and numerical tables are complete for all three levels.
Margin distribution trends are shown; three SIR points are insufficient to fit a precise decision-flip threshold.
WGN and all three DEMAND environments are complete.

Retain both own and the original proposal's target definitions in full; nominal power is not complete acoustic matching. Add joint selection using spectral overlap, time-frequency masking and temporal overlap; disclose that about 9–10.5% of targets are retained.

Use a 40 dB active-frame definition and record active-region overlap; do not attribute the own-region change to an explicit instructor instruction. Include temporal overlap and spectra within target-active frames; no alignment changes or new time-shift experiments were performed.
Recompute after generation and store in the manifest; explicitly exclude zero-energy pairs with undefined ratios.
Retain all 2,000 clips, 50 classes and five folds.
Some original preprocessing is class-dependent; also disclose source IDs spanning folds and uncertainty about external pretraining.
One seed in the core experiment; the extension completes seeds 5305, 5306 and 5307.

items.recommendation: Prioritise failure analysis over architecture tuning for leaderboard performance
items.assessment: Retain the small CNN and focus extensions on interference, augmentation transfer and diagnostics.

items.recommendation: Treat ordinary augmentation as an extension
items.assessment: Complete clean-trained robustness first, followed by separate WGN-augmented training.

items.recommendation: Test transfer from ordinary augmentation to semantic interference
items.assessment: Evaluate SVM/CNN under both power definitions.

items.recommendation: Treat augmentation transfer as a hypothesis to test
items.assessment: Observed transfer is limited; retain uncertainty and negative findings.
Both augmentation types are complete for SVM and for all three CNN seeds.
Retain core results and name/report extensions separately.
Analyse 8 feature groups separately, using the corresponding training-fold standard deviations.

items.recommendation: Is displacement magnitude sufficient to explain failure?
items.assessment: Compare displacement and classification for matched targets; retain uncontrolled explanations such as direction and class boundaries.
Save 256-dimensional penultimate-layer vectors and use cosine distance.
Save 512-dimensional vectors, including AUC for the association between displacement and errors.

items.recommendation: Do not compare absolute distances across architectures
items.assessment: Use separate panels and explain the different representation geometries.

items.recommendation: Inspect text scores for other competing classes
items.assessment: Save the top 3 other classes; this revision adds changes in the strongest other-class score and a table of the three prediction destinations. Exact top-1/2/3/5 from all 50 class scores is complete, including the existing fixed prompt ensemble.
Use a fixed template in the core experiment; the separate fixed prompt ensemble is not selected using test labels.

items.recommendation: PAT as an optional modern extension
items.assessment: Only reuse the released template list for fixed averaging; full mutual feedback and local audio alignment are not implemented.
Pin the source commit and template provenance, and report differences from full PAT.
Changes from fixed text readout have been evaluated; full PAT's alignment mechanism has not.
PAT was not trained, and the prompt-ensemble ablation is not described as full PAT.
Cited but not reproduced; the instructor explicitly did not require reproduction.
Four interference panels and three systems; both own/target figure sets are in the repository.
Conditions and denominators are explicit; 1/49 is only a reference for uniformly distributed incorrect labels.
Retain each model's own score scale.
Relative F1 loss uses the same retained targets; distinguish the ratio of means from foldwise ratios.
Compare gain-matched controls and mixtures, split by correct/incorrect predictions; make no causal claim.
Select examples by observed counts; captions distinguish existing confusion from newly induced capture.
Retain the original microbenchmark and state its definition; add two rounds of cost measurements on balanced samples.
Use the same machine, one thread and batch 1; explain preprocessing/inference boundaries and list one-off text preparation separately.

items.recommendation: Do not include CLAP pretraining in local inference cost
items.assessment: Explain the external training advantage; do not claim a fair comparison of lifetime costs.
Pin the official snapshot and metadata.
Cite the log-Mel CNN approach; do not reproduce the historical architecture layer by layer, which the instructor did not require.
Pin the checkpoint, use the official tensor path and frozen inference, and record hashes and environments.
Reviewed and used for an explicitly named prompt-ensemble ablation; the full algorithm has not been reproduced.
Clean five-fold evaluation, custom STFT and the course MATLAB comparison are complete.
Clean five-fold evaluation and the three-seed extension are complete.
WGN/DEMAND mixing and evaluation on identical inputs are complete.
Engineering verification and 24 examples are complete; successful audio loading is not presented as a human listening assessment.
Clean and full own/target evaluations are complete, with scores and vectors cached.
F1, accuracy, degradation, capture, margin and representation displacement are complete.
Ordinary augmentation is complete, with semantic augmentation and a fixed prompt ensemble added.
The original classical references, CLAP and PAT are included in the formal report draft.
Primary sources for Mix-CLAP and RSA-Bench have been checked, and task boundaries are noted.
Three systems, five folds, all interference conditions and all metrics are covered.
No CLAP training/fine-tuning, Mix-CLAP reproduction or exhaustive pairing was performed.
Code, results, figures and examples are in feature/interference and the PR; public Pages was published from gh-pages and download hashes were checked. main has not yet been merged.

Study different failure modes under acoustic corruption and label competition; the experiments do not causally isolate semantics. Both closing analyses are complete; retain the interpretive boundaries between readout, acoustics and unmeasured salience, with no further models or datasets.
